summary: William Stede was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held a post at the University of London and SOAS from circa 1928 to 1949.

William Theodore de Bary worked in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University, Harvard University, and the U.S. Navy Japanese Language School, and was Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia from 1953 to 2017.

William Van Gordon is a researcher in religious and Buddhist studies. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and was a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University in 2015.

William Ward worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett in 1797, served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission from circa 1799 to 1823, and founded Serampore College in 1818.

William Wilson Hunter was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Glasgow, University of Paris, and University of Bonn. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1862–1887) and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta in 1886.
William Witherle Lawrence studied at Harvard University (~1898–1903). He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1899–1900) and Harvard University (~1900–1903).

William Woodville Rockhill specialized in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873), and under Léon Feer and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1876–1884).

William Wright was a linguist who studied at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He held posts at UCL, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum (1861–1870), and was Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge (1870–1889).

Willibald Kirfel was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He worked at Bonn University Library (1911–1921) and served as a librarian, privatdozent, and professor at the University of Bonn starting in 1920 and 1922.

Wilt L. Idema is a Sinologist who earned degrees at Leiden University under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé. He held posts as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden University (1976–1999) and Harvard University (2000–2013).
Win Than Tun is a historian who studied at the National University of Singapore under Myo Myint.

Winfred P. Lehmann worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1941) and served on the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin from circa 1949 to 1986.
Winfred Robert Martin was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Wing-tsit Chan was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Harvard University (~1924–1929). He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1937–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who studied at Cornell and the University of Chicago. She held posts at Washington and Lee University, the University of Chicago, University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington.
Winston Kyan is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Hung Wu and Linda Seidel.

Wolf Singer studied at the University of Munich (~1962–1968). He held posts at Technical University of Munich, Goethe University Frankfurt, Ernst Strüngmann Institute, and the Max Planck Institute for Brain Research (~1981–2011).

Wolfgang Franke worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Hamburg, he taught at Sichuan University, Peking University, and held the Sinology chair at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1977).

Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD under Richard Hauschild at the University of Jena. He held posts at Jena, the University of Greifswald, and served as Professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).

Wolfgang Schultz was a scholar of philosophy and history who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. He worked at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and was Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.
